finding: Mandatory verification exists, but not on the path that loads a package. The registry harness makes it a precondition of resolution - signature then digest, refuse-and-continue, and a deliberate breakage that downgrades the digest check to a warning is what makes its gate fail - which is exactly the aligned behaviour. The loading interface next to it has no signature concept at all (0 occurrences across its interface, caller and registry adapter); its registry adapter's own docstring says it "verifies the digest the registry reports" but the code only recomputes a digest over whatever bytes came back and compares it to nothing, so a tampered record would resolve; the load is not a policy decision anywhere (the enforcement chain's slots are admission, dispatch and call, with no package-resolution point); and the run ledger's capability-call record for a load names the identity and the tiers but carries no version, digest or signature field, so an artifact cannot be traced to the package bytes that shaped it.
gap: No digest match and no signature check precede a load: verification lives in a separate registry interface that the loader never calls, and the loader's own digest is descriptive, not verifying (nothing is compared, so a mismatch cannot refuse). No policy decision is taken at resolution or load, and no provenance statement or ledger record names the version or digest of the packages in force when an artifact was produced.

gap: Composition is undefined: no example loads two packages, so there is no ordering, no combined resident cost and no stated resolution when two packages contradict each other - only last-writer-wins by default. evidence.quote: a change is a new version, never an edit
the packaging format publishes no explicit version

finding: The version half of the contract exists and is exercised: semantic versions are ordered and parsed, a constraint walks candidates newest-first without falling outside the range, republishing a version already published is refused so a change cannot be shipped as an edit, and a rollback is a resolution of the earlier record rather than a mutation - 20 gate checks pass on it. It is nominal in the place it would have to bite. No package this repository ships carries a version: the skill schema has no version property, the packaging format publishes none, and the registry adapter mints a synthetic 1.0.0 for every skill on first scan, so a breaking change to a real package (the fold, which rewrote 103 packages into 28 and dropped names consumers had loaded) was shipped by editing the package in place with no signal a consumer could read before loading. Withdrawal does not exist at all: no operation withdraws or deprecates a version, so a bad version cannot be taken back and a consumer pinned to one gets no refusal, deterministic or otherwise.
gap: Packages are unversioned in practice - no version field in the format or the schema, and a synthetic 1.0.0 assigned at scan time - so a breaking change is invisible before load and is shipped by editing in place. There is no withdraw or deprecate operation anywhere, and therefore no defined resolution behaviour for a consumer pinned to a withdrawn version.
